title: Jeonbok Gui Grilled Abalone
shortDescription: Cleaned abalone is removed from the shell, trimmed, scored, and grilled briefly with garlic-sesame seasoning until firm and safely cooked.
culturalContext: Jeonbok gui refers to grilled abalone in Korean cooking. Cleaning, whether viscera are used, seasoning, shell presentation, and tenderness vary; this conservative draft discards viscera and requires market and cultural review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Wide blunt spoon or abalone tool
Outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill

instructions.heading: Verify source and vitality
instructions.action: Buy labeled live abalone from a reputable source, keep cold, and reject cracked shells, off odor, or nonresponsive flesh.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Abalone respond to touch and smell mild.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not use dead, damaged, unverified, or temperature-abused shellfish.

instructions.heading: Scrub and remove safely
instructions.action: Scrub shells, wear a cut-resistant glove, and use a blunt tool to separate each abalone from its shell.
instructions.safetyNote: Shell edges and tools can cut; keep the supporting hand protected.

instructions.heading: Trim and clean
instructions.action: Remove and discard viscera and mouthparts, scrub dark edges, rinse briefly, dry, and score the foot shallowly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Only clean firm foot meat remains.
instructions.safetyNote: This draft does not use viscera; sanitize the board and tools after cleaning.

instructions.heading: Season and preheat
instructions.action: Mix oil, garlic, soy, and sesame oil; coat abalone lightly and preheat a clean grill tray over medium-high.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Abalone have a thin coating and the tray is hot.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep seasoning tools used on raw abalone away from cooked food.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Grill scored-side down, turn once, and cook until firm, opaque, lightly browned, and 145°F / 63°C in representative thick pieces.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean tongs and thermometer after the final turn.

instructions.heading: Slice and serve
instructions.action: Rest 2 minutes, slice with a clean knife into manageable pieces, and serve on clean shells only if shells were separately scrubbed and sanitized.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are manageable and served cleanly.
instructions.safetyNote: Abalone can be chewy and a choking risk; cut appropriately for diners.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill with a stable lightly oiled tray over medium-high heat; keep raw and cooked zones separate.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in representative thick abalone pieces, pending qualified shellfish review.
foodSafetyNotes: Buy labeled live abalone from a reputable source and keep cold.
Protect hands from sharp shells and clean away viscera and mouthparts.
Prevent raw-shellfish cross-contact and cook to 145°F / 63°C pending review.
Cut chewy flesh into manageable pieces to reduce choking risk.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains shellfish, soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify labels.

substitutions: Do not substitute canned or frozen abalone without a separate process.
ingredientSourcing: Buy labeled live farmed abalone from a reputable seafood dealer and retain source information.
makeAhead: Clean immediately before cooking; seasoning may be mixed 1 day ahead and refrigerated.
storage: Refrigerate cooked abalone within 2 hours and use within 2 days pending review.
reheating: Reheat gently to 165°F / 74°C until steaming; overcooking may toughen it.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window.
servingSuggestions: Serve sliced with rice and fresh sides.

faq.question: Can I use the viscera?
faq.answer: Not in this conservative draft; viscera use requires separate cultural and safety review.

faq.question: Why cut it after grilling?
faq.answer: Abalone is chewy, so manageable slices reduce choking risk.

metaDescription: Make jeonbok gui with labeled live abalone, cut-safe cleaning, discarded viscera, cross-contact controls, a 145°F / 63°C check, and manageable slicing.

buyingCues: Abalone are live and responsive with intact shells and mild odor.
Source label identifies seller and product.
Product is cold and has not been temperature abused.
seafoodPreparation.thawing: Not applicable; this draft uses live abalone only.
seafoodPreparation.cleaningOrShellPreparation: With cut protection, scrub shell, remove meat using a blunt tool, discard viscera and mouthparts, scrub dark edges, rinse briefly, dry, and sanitize tools.
seafoodPreparation.drying: Pat cleaned foot meat dry with disposable towels and discard towels immediately.
seafoodPreparation.scoringOrSkewering: Score the foot shallowly in a crosshatch without cutting through.
seafoodPreparation.grillSurfacePreparation: Preheat and lightly oil a stable grill tray.
seafoodPreparation.stickingPrevention: Dry well, oil lightly, and turn only after the scored surface releases.
seafoodPreparation.approximateTime: 6 to 8 minutes depending on size; thermometer verification controls.
seafoodPreparation.applicableTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in representative thick pieces pending qualified review.
seafoodPreparation.shellOpeningAndDiscardGuidance: Not applicable to abalone; reject nonresponsive live product before preparation.
crossContactNotes: Use a dedicated raw-shellfish board and tools.
Sanitize the sink and work area after cleaning.
Use clean tongs, thermometer, knife, and platter for cooked abalone.
